## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical skills in Secrets management, startup behavior, and zero-downtime updates in Kubernetes—core for data-facing workloads in Snowflake and Nvidia contexts.

## Key Concepts

- Kubernetes Secrets and rotation
- Pod startup and readiness checks
- Rolling updates / canary deployments
- Observability and latency SLAs (P95 metric targets)

## Code Example

```bash
# Create rotated secret
kubectl create secret generic db-credentials-v2 --from-literal=password='NEW_PASSWORD'

# Surface the secret used by the deployment
kubectl get pod <pod> -o jsonpath='{.spec.volumes[*].secret.secretName}'

# Point the deployment at the new secret (zero-downtime rollout)
kubectl patch deployment/db-api -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"volumes":[{"name":"db-creds","secret":{"secretName":"db-credentials-v2"}}]}}}}'

# Monitor rollout progress
kubectl rollout status deployment/db-api
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you automate secret rotation with no downtime?
- What metrics would confirm P95 latency stays under 180 ms during the rollout?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests DNS resolution inside a cluster and safe rollback.

- CoreDNS ConfigMap, Corefile
- in-cluster DNS lookups, nslookup/dig
- Canary rollouts, zero-downtime

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: coredns
  namespace: kube-system
data:
  Corefile: |
    .:53 {
      errors
      cache 30
      forward . 8.8.8.8
      health
      kubernetes cluster.local in-addr.arpa ip6.arpa {
        fallthrough
      }
    }
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to diagnose admission webhook performance bottlenecks under load and implement safe rollout strategies while maintaining service availability.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes admission webhooks and ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
- API server latency metrics and performance monitoring
- Canary deployment strategies with traffic shifting
- Timeout configuration and SLA management
- P95 latency thresholds and performance validation

## Code Example
```bash
# Verify webhook configuration
kubectl get validatingwebhookconfigurations
kubectl describe validatingwebhookconfigurations <webhook-name>

# Inspect webhook pods and logs
kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l app=quota-webhook
kubectl logs -n kube-system -l app=quota-webhook --tail=200

# Measure API server latency
curl -s http://<apiserver>/metrics | grep apiserver_request_latencies_seconds

# Canary rollout with updated timeout
kubectl patch deployment quota-webhook -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"quota-webhook","env":[{"name":"WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT","value":"180s"}]}]}}}}'
```

## Key Concepts
- Vault integration with Kubernetes and per-tenant leases
- Canary rollouts with rollback safety
- Tenant-scoped credentials TTL and renewal behavior
- Latency validation with Prometheus-style queries

## Code Example

```javascript
// Diagnostic steps in shell
kubectl get pods -n kcsa-prod
kubectl exec <pod> -- sh -lc 'vault status; vault kv get secret/tenants/tenantA'
kubectl rollout restart deployment/data-api-gateway-canary
kubectl rollout status deployment/data-api-gateway-canary
```
